articles.heading: Rate of Play
articles.content:
For a game to be rated by FIDE the rate of play must satisfy the following conditions:

Standard chess: The time control must allow at least 60 minutes for each player to complete all moves. More precisely, the total allotted time T for each player must satisfy: T ≥ 60 minutes, where T = basic time + (increment × 60).

Rapid chess: 10 ≤ T < 60 minutes for each player.

Blitz chess: 3 ≤ T < 10 minutes for each player.

Games not satisfying these time controls are not eligible for FIDE rating.

Note: Standard, Rapid and Blitz rating lists are maintained separately. A game played under rapid or blitz time controls affects only the respective rapid or blitz rating, not the standard rating.

Example: A time control of 15 minutes + 10 seconds increment gives T = 15 + (10 × 60)/60 = 15 + 10 = 25 minutes, which qualifies as rapid.

articles.heading: Laws to be Followed
articles.content:
All rated games must be played in accordance with the FIDE Laws of Chess. Any game played under conditions that deviate from the Laws of Chess without FIDE authorisation cannot be submitted for rating.

The arbiter is responsible for ensuring that the Laws are followed throughout the event. In particular:
- Games must be played with the correct starting position
- Clock settings must comply with the announced time control
- Players must record their moves (except in rapid and blitz events where recording is optional)
- Forfeit wins count for rating only if the opponent's results in the tournament are also submitted

Organisers who submit results for games not played under the Laws of Chess risk having those events removed from the rating list and may be subject to sanctions.

articles.heading: Hours of Play
articles.content:
Games must be played at the announced times and on the announced dates. Significant deviations must be notified to FIDE. The arbiter must record all times of play accurately on the tournament report.

An event with games played on different days from those announced, or with the round schedule significantly altered, may be subject to rating restrictions or rejection. The Chief Arbiter must document any deviations in the tournament report and provide reasons.

For events where pairings software generates a time-stamped pairing file, the arbiter should retain these files for verification purposes in the event of a dispute.

articles.heading: Reporting Frequency
articles.content:
All rated events must be reported to FIDE within two months of the end of the event. Failure to report within this period may result in the event not being rated.

The Chief Arbiter is responsible for submitting the rating report in the prescribed format using FIDE-approved software. Reports must be submitted electronically through the FIDE Online Arena or by the designated reporting system.

Required information in the report:
- Tournament name, location, dates
- FIDE ID of all participants
- Ratings of all participants at the start of the event
- All results (including forfeits and byes treated correctly)
- Chief Arbiter's name and FIDE ID
- Signature/certification by the Chief Arbiter

National federations are required to upload reports promptly. Persistent failure to report may result in the federation's events being denied rating status.

articles.heading: Unplayed Games
articles.content:
Unplayed games (forfeits, byes, withdrawals) are treated as follows for rating purposes:

Forfeit wins (+/-): A forfeit win counts for rating only if the opponent has played at least one rated game in the tournament.

Forfeit losses (-/+): Count for rating only if the player has played at least one rated game in the tournament.

Full-point byes (BYE=1): These are not rated.

Half-point byes (BYE=0.5): These are not rated.

Withdrawals: If a player withdraws having completed fewer than 50% of their scheduled games, their results (and the results of their opponents against them) may be excluded from the rating calculation. If 50% or more games are completed, all results stand.

Dual forfeits (both players forfeit): Not rated for either player.

The arbiter must clearly distinguish between played and unplayed games on the rating report. Incorrect treatment of unplayed games is a common source of rating report errors.

articles.heading: The Working of the FIDE Rating System
articles.content:
The FIDE rating system is based on the Elo system, developed by Professor Arpad Elo.

Expected score: For a game between a player rated Ra and an opponent rated Rb, the expected score for the player is:
We = 1 / (1 + 10^((Rb-Ra)/400))

Rating change: After a game or tournament, the rating change is:
ΔR = K × (W - We)
where:
- K is the development coefficient
- W is the actual score achieved
- We is the expected score

K-factors:
- K = 40: for new players until they have played 30 rated games AND until the end of the calendar year in which they first reached a published standard rating
- K = 20: for players with a published rating below 2400
- K = 10: for players who have had a published rating of 2400 or more at any time

Rapid and Blitz: K = 20 for all players in rapid and blitz rating calculations.

Performance rating: The performance rating of a player in a tournament is the average rating of opponents adjusted for the score achieved. It is used for title norm calculations.

articles.heading: Reporting Procedures
articles.content:
The organiser must submit a complete rating report containing:
- A list of all players with FIDE IDs, federation codes, titles, and ratings at the start of the event
- All pairings and results in the prescribed format (crosstable or round-by-round)
- Correct treatment of unplayed games (forfeits, byes, withdrawals)
- The Chief Arbiter's FIDE ID and certification

For FIDE-rated tournaments, reports are submitted through the National Federation's Rating Officer, who uploads them to the FIDE Rating Server.

Common errors to avoid:
- Using outdated FIDE IDs or incorrect player names
- Submitting ratings from the wrong list
- Failing to mark forfeit wins/losses correctly
- Missing the submission deadline

For events yielding title norms, additional documentation (IT1 norm certificate forms) must be submitted separately through the title application process.

articles.heading: Inclusion in the Rating List and FIDE Rapid & Blitz Regulations
articles.content:
For a player to receive an initial FIDE standard rating, they must play at least 5 rated games against rated opponents in the same rating period.

Once rated, a player's rating is updated in each bi-monthly rating list provided they have played at least one rated game during the period.

FIDE Rapid Rating Regulations:
- Minimum rate of play: 10 minutes ≤ T < 60 minutes
- From 1 December 2024: a minimum of 5 games against rated opponents is required for an initial rapid rating
- Rapid rating uses K = 20 for all players

FIDE Blitz Rating Regulations:
- Minimum rate of play: 3 minutes ≤ T < 10 minutes  
- From 1 December 2024: a minimum of 5 games against rated opponents is required for an initial blitz rating
- Blitz rating uses K = 20 for all players

Rapid and blitz ratings are published on separate FIDE rating lists and maintained independently from standard ratings. The FIDE rating lists for standard, rapid and blitz are updated separately on different schedules.
